questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes feature scaling?

options.text: Transforming features to a common scale to improve algorithm performance.
Selecting only the most important features.

questions.explanation: Feature scaling standardizes or normalizes values so that algorithms sensitive to magnitude work properly.

questions.prompt: When is it more appropriate to use one-hot encoding instead of label encoding for a categorical variable?

options.text: When the variable has an inherent order.
When the variable has many unique categories.
When the variable is ordinal and has no natural order.
When the variable is nominal with a small number of categories.

questions.explanation: One-hot encoding avoids imposing arbitrary numeric relationships and works best for nominal categories with limited cardinality.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of creating polynomial interaction features in a regression model?

options.text: To reduce dimensionality by combining features.
To capture non-linear relationships between predictors.
To encode categorical variables into binary form.
To handle missing data by creating new features.

questions.explanation: Polynomial terms allow the model to learn interactions and curvature, improving fit for non-linear patterns.
